limitations: Known token totals exclude requests lacking response usage; unknown tokens are not zero.

Actor accounting covers persisted receipts. Abruptly interrupted requests may leave no receipt, so all-attempt actor token totals are observed lower bounds rather than an exhaustive backend billing ledger.
Actor requests can contain transport retries; receipts count metered logical requests, not unobserved backend attempts.
Actor client and backend latencies overlap across candidates and episodes; their sums are not GPU time or episode wall time.

Nine committed episodes snapshot actor client latency before all failing sibling requests finish. Final receipt latency includes this tail; token and request counts reconcile exactly. The saved episode wall-time is time to result, not time until every sibling request is quiescent.
Episode elapsed time includes browser, generation, selection, judging, and artifact work; logging-phase differences affect it.
Both arms share each allocation and GPU; exact per-arm GPU-hours/FLOPs are unavailable.
Selector receipt base costs omit uncertain cache-write surcharge; ledgers conservatively charge upper usage costs, plus unresolved reservations. Neither is a provider invoice.
All-attempt costs include interrupted/uncommitted episodes; committed means use only the final selected record per task and arm.
Common-phase results are sensitivity subsets; full600 remains the primary cohort.
Both execution phases use the same awaited logging policy. Initial/recovery source sensitivity separately exposes retry and error-handling repairs; its task subsets are not randomly assigned.
Actor backend e2e latency is optional; only receipts carrying it contribute to its denominator.
